query: How long do I have to return a laptop bought on the business plan?

passages.text: Laptop accessory returns: any laptop accessory bought alongside a laptop may be returned within 90 days of the laptop order date, provided the accessory is unopened.
Business plan hardware may be sent back for a full credit up to 45 days after it arrives at the delivery address on the order.
Consumer plan customers have 30 days from delivery to request a return for any device, including laptops and tablets.
Under the 2023 terms of service, the hardware return window for all plans was 14 days. Those terms were replaced and apply only to orders placed before the migration.
To start a return you need an RMA number. Open the order in the admin console, choose Request return, and a prepaid label is emailed to the billing contact.
Laptops are returned to our Utrecht depot. Returned laptops are wiped, graded, and either refurbished or recycled depending on the grade.
Business plan seats are billed annually in advance. Seat reductions take effect at the next renewal and are not refunded mid-term.
Our Lisbon office is on the fourth floor of Rua do Alecrim 26 and reception opens at nine on weekdays.
Damaged-on-arrival laptops are handled by the warranty process, not the returns process, and have no fixed window as long as the damage is reported on receipt.
Return shipping is free on the business plan. Consumer plan returns deduct a flat handling fee from the refund unless the item was faulty.

query: Why does the invoice export job time out on large accounts?

passages.text: The invoice import job times out when a CSV exceeds 50 MB. Split the file and re-run the import; the importer streams but the validation pass does not.

The XLSX serialiser builds the whole workbook in memory. Above roughly 500 line items the worker exceeds its 30 second budget and the supervisor kills it mid-write, which surfaces to the user as a spinner that never resolves.
Export jobs run on the batch queue with two retries and exponential backoff. A killed worker is retried, and a job that fails three times is moved to the dead letter queue.
In the analytics product, the export job writes directly to object storage and has no worker time limit, so large exports there complete normally.
Invoices are generated nightly for accounts on metered billing. Generation is unrelated to export and runs on a separate schedule.
Workaround for affected customers: export as CSV rather than XLSX. The CSV writer streams row by row and has no memory ceiling.
Large accounts are defined in the pricing docs as those above 10,000 monthly active seats. This is a billing classification and has no effect on job scheduling.
The export button was moved into the actions menu in the December release following usability feedback.
Worker time limits are configured per queue in deploy/queues.yaml. The batch queue is currently 30 seconds; raising it requires a platform review because the same pool serves webhooks.
A spinner that never resolves usually means the request completed with a non-JSON body. The front end waits on a parse that never succeeds and shows no error.

query: What happens if nobody acknowledges a page after ten minutes?

passages.text: Acknowledgement is recorded when the responder taps Ack in the mobile app or replies ACK to the SMS. The timer stops at that point.
If the primary responder has not acknowledged, the page escalates to the secondary on the rotation, and then to the engineering manager on the third notification.
Escalation policies are configured per service. Ours uses a ten minute step, so each unacknowledged notification moves one level up the chain.
Ten minutes is also the window in which a deploy can be rolled back automatically before the canary is promoted. This is a deploy setting and has nothing to do with paging.
Pages are delivered by push, SMS and phone call in that order, with each channel tried before the next.
The on-call rotation runs weekly, handing over at ten on Monday morning. Handover notes go in the runbook channel.
Acknowledging a page does not resolve the incident. A page that is acknowledged but not resolved within an hour re-notifies the same responder.
If the entire rotation fails to acknowledge, the policy terminates at the engineering manager and the incident is posted to the leadership channel with no further escalation.
Our paging vendor bills per notification delivered. SMS and phone notifications cost more than push, which is why push is tried first.
Alert rules live in the monitoring repo. Changing a threshold there changes when a page fires, not what happens after one fires.
